kept.name: paddleocr
kept.reason: Covers both of your local tiers: PP-StructureV3 is a PDF-to-markdown pipeline that runs on CPU, and PaddleOCR-VL is a 0.9B vision model small enough for a 16 GB GPU.

kept.name: chandra-ocr
kept.reason: Vision model that turns PDFs into markdown or HTML, with strong math and table handling. Good small-GPU candidate for complex papers; check the modified OpenRAIL-M weights license.

kept.name: ovisocr2
kept.reason: 0.8B end-to-end page-to-markdown model (LaTeX formulas, HTML tables, figure regions) with published OmniDocBench and PureDocBench scores. Strong 16 GB GPU candidate.

kept.name: jina-ocr-v1
kept.reason: Document-to-markdown model (3.4B total, 570M active) with OmniDocBench and olmOCR-Bench scores. Also has a hosted Reader API, so it fits both the small-GPU and hosted tiers. Weights are non-commercial (CC BY-NC).

kept.name: olmocr
kept.reason: AI2's 7B PDF-to-markdown model, plus a benchmark with 7K+ test cases you could reuse to score the other approaches.

kept.name: mineru
kept.reason: Open-source parser that converts PDFs to markdown, with four quality tiers and a combined vision-model/OCR engine. It runs locally on CPU or GPU, so it can be tested at more than one tier.

kept.name: docling-mcp
kept.reason: Docling (IBM's open-source document converter) wrapped as an MCP server. Docling is a standard CPU baseline for layout and table-structure parsing.

kept.name: markitdown
kept.reason: Microsoft's lightweight PDF-to-markdown converter. Useful as the simplest CPU baseline in the comparison.

kept.name: opendataloader-pdf
kept.reason: Top-benchmarked open-source PDF parser that outputs markdown and handles formulas. The entry already flags it for piloting on bioinformatics papers.

kept.name: unstructured
kept.reason: Widely used tool that splits PDFs into elements such as titles, text and tables, with layout models and OCR. Offers both a local CPU parser and a hosted API.

kept.name: meridian
kept.reason: Reference GPU setup: Docling for layout plus Qwen3-VL on vLLM for tables, figures and formulas, with measured throughput. Useful for designing a hybrid pipeline.

kept.name: amazon-textract-textractor
kept.reason: Python wrapper around Amazon Textract. Candidate for the hosted-API tier, especially for extracting tables.

kept.name: llama-index
kept.reason: Linked to LlamaParse, LlamaIndex's commercial PDF-parsing service, which is a candidate for the hosted-API tier.

kept.name: parsebench
kept.reason: Benchmark that scores document parsers on text, formatting, tables, charts and page attribution. Directly relevant to how you score results.

kept.name: extractbench
kept.reason: Benchmark with a fixed F1 metric and no LLM judge. Gives you a lesson on how to score fairly against an LLM agent baseline.

kept.name: isaacflath-ocr-guides
kept.reason: Blog series on choosing OCR models, using vision models for OCR, quantization and pipeline design. Practical lessons for the 16 GB GPU tier.

kept.name: pdf-mcp
kept.reason: MCP server that gives an agent tools to pull tables, images and charts from PDFs and handle multi-column layouts. Relevant to how the LLM agent baseline accesses PDFs.

kept.name: seb-ocr
kept.reason: Working OCR pipeline built on Gemini, with rate limiting and caching. Useful setup patterns for the hosted-API tier.

kept.name: book-to-skill
kept.reason: Existing entry for extracting text, tables and figures from computational biology methods PDFs (mentions Docling). Close to your use case.

kept.name: armorocr
kept.reason: Qwen3-VL-8B OCR model and benchmark focused on robustness to hard or distorted inputs. Possible lesson for evaluating difficult scans and figures.

kept.name: llmfit
kept.reason: Tool that checks which models fit your hardware. Useful for choosing and sizing vision models on a 16 GB GPU.

kept.name: sglang
kept.reason: Serving framework for vision models, an alternative to vLLM. Useful for running the small vision models locally.
